title: Fix what release 4.2 shipped in its class files

blocks.text: Release 4.2 of the invoicing module went out with three complaints:

items: a partner ran `javap -v` on the released jar and read one of the team's review notes, word for word, in `InvoiceService`'s class file;
the coverage report suddenly counts `InvoiceMapper`, which the mapper generator writes and the coverage tool is supposed to leave out (the tool reads compiled `.class` files, never sources);

blocks.text: All three annotations are declared in `src/main/java/practice/Invoicing.java`, each with a `TODO` above the retention it shipped with. Give each the retention its reader needs, then write `cacheSeconds(Class<?>)`, which the cache layer calls on every service class at start-up: each method the class declares with `@Cached`, by name, with its seconds.
About eight lines in total. The tests read the compiled class files the same way the coverage tool does, and call `cacheSeconds` on classes of their own.

cases.says: the cache settings of InvoiceService name each @Cached method with its seconds
the cache settings work for another class compiled against the same annotation, and are empty for a class with none
the compiled InvoiceService class holds neither the review note's text nor its annotation
the compiled InvoiceMapper class still carries the @Generated mark the coverage tool looks for

origin.section: SOURCE Stops at the Compiler, CLASS Stops in the Class File, Only RUNTIME Reaches Reflection

concepts: A CLASS annotation ships in the class file with its values, so only SOURCE keeps it out of the jar, and a tool that reads class files needs CLASS or RUNTIME.
javac drops a SOURCE annotation, writes a CLASS annotation to RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations and a RUNTIME one to RuntimeVisibleAnnotations; only the last is returned by reflection.
